Subject: Request: HSM operator transcripts + emergency rewrap runbook

Hi Ben,

We're preparing for a cross-region tenant migration and the SIG/SOC2 assessor has asked for granular evidence around key custody and any emergency rewrap procedures. Specifically they want: 
- HSM operator shift logs (UTC timestamps) covering the last 30 days for any operator-initiated commands affecting wrap/unwrap or KEK material
- The emergency rewrap runbook that your ops team would execute (step-by-step, with required approvals and who holds which keys)
- Signed operator acknowledgement/transcripts for any rewrap or KEK change during that window

Can Redwood provide these as a packaged deliverable? Redactions of customer identifiers are fine, but the assessor needs operator IDs, timestamps, and the cryptographic event records. Also please include a high-level note on in-transit and at-rest envelope encryption behaviors during a rewrap (expected svc interruption, fallback) so we can map risk.

We'd like this by EOD May 28 if possible — the assessor will review on May 29. If you need a different format (raw audit CSV vs redacted PDF), tell us.

Thanks,

Attachment stubs included here: 
- hsm_shiftlog_20290521.csv (event-level HSM audit trail; columns: timestamp_utc, operator_id, command, command_args_redacted, response_code)
- rewrap_playbook_v1.2.pdf (step-by-step emergency KEK rewrap; includes approval matrix and required HSM policy changes)
- operator_signatures_202905.zip (PGP-signed manifest + per-operator signature files)

Quick technical notes:
- The rewrap playbook assumes envelope encryption using tenant KEKs wrapped by a cluster KEK stored on the HSM. During the rewrap we perform a rolling KEK unwrap/rewrap with a 2-minute per-node handover window; no full-system downtime is required.
- In-transit encryption remains TLS 1.3 (AES-GCM); all rewrap traffic is initiated over authenticated mTLS channels to HSM controllers.
- At-rest: data is double-encrypted (tenant envelope + disk encryption). A KEK rotation only replaces envelope wrapping keys; payload ciphertext remains unchanged.
- When an emergency rewrap is executed we mark affected tokens as 'rewrap_pending' and transparently rewrap on the next token unwrap call; TTLs are not reset. The playbook describes the fallback path (automated bypass to read-only mode) if operator errors are detected.

SHA256 checksums: 
- hsm_shiftlog_20290521.csv: 9f2b3c1a4d8e... (truncated)
- rewrap_playbook_v1.2.pdf: a5d4f7c8b2e3... (truncated)

Let me know if you need a redacted CSV (we can remove tenant ids but will keep operator and event details).
